text:
alex: Kicking off Zephyr Logistics POC. They need streaming chat + function/tool calling, STRICT line-delimited JSON (NDJSON) per event for downstream ingestion, SAML SSO, customer-managed KMS/BYOK, and mutual-TLS webhooks for callbacks to their internal endpoints. POC hosted, browser clients + server workers, ephemeral creds preferred in browser. Also they asked for telemetry: trace_id per request and a sample of request-level cost telemetry.

meera: Quick clarifiers: 1) Are callbacks one-way webhooks (server->customer) or do we need mutual auth both ways? 2) Do they require encrypted payloads at rest with their KMS?

alex: They explicitly want mutual-TLS for outgoing callbacks and want payloads encrypted at rest with a customer key when stored. SOC2 required; they'll need report and a short security appendix.

spencer: Tech notes: SDK support: Node/Python stable for streaming + function calls. Go SDK has an alpha websocket client (good for server agents). Browser: SSE (EventSource) is simplest for NDJSON chunking; websockets for server agents if you need bi-directional. For NDJSON we emit event lines like: `event: message\ndata: {"type":"function_call","name":"route_shipment","args":{...}}\n` and finalizers send a `state: complete` line.

spencer: SSE example (browser):
```js
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream?ndjson=true', { headers:{ Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } });
es.onmessage = (e)=>{ try { const obj = JSON.parse(e.data); /* handle */ } catch(e) { /* partial chunk handling*/ } };
// Keepalive for Safari: poll /ping every 20s or use server-sent comment pings
```

meera: Important blockers: hosted+BYOK+mutual-TLS implies enterprise ops for outbound cert management; legal LOA + KMS attestation required. For customer-managed-at-rest encryption we need Dedicated/Private or a signed architecture addendum. Expect 2-3 week lead time for BYOK + mTLS setup.

alex: They stressed resumable streams on reconnect so product pages don't lose state. Any recommended approach?

spencer: Two patterns: 1) resumable_id returned on stream start; reconnect with ?resumable_id & offset; 2) sequence numbers on each NDJSON line so client can request missing ranges after reconnect. We have a resumable prototype that returns resumable_id in a control event. Pseudocode: 
```js
// initial open
// receives: { "control":"resumable_id","id":"r-abc123" }
// on reconnect: EventSource('/v1/chat/stream?resumable_id=r-abc123', { headers:{ Authorization:`Bearer ${NEW}` } });
```
Works well with token rotation. Note: Safari idle timeout requires sending comment pings to keep connection alive.

meera: Known SDK caveat: browser SSE + short-lived creds can lead to 401/reconnect loops if the client aggressively retries without fetching a refreshed token. Workarounds: broker tokens via a server endpoint that handles refresh, or use resumable_id so reconnects are cheap. Patch PR #2001 adds a client helper to gracefully retry once after refresh and backoff.

spencer: Another enterprise ask: they want our server to initiate outbound mutual-TLS to their webhook and validate their client cert for callbacks. That requires storing client cert bundles per customer and an ops playbook for cert rotation. We can support it on Dedicated or an enterprise managed offering.

security-bot: Hosted+BYOK+outbound mTLS requires enterprise plan. We can provide SOC2 under NDA. For E2E customer-managed at-rest encryption we recommend Dedicated/Private; hosted with BYOK still stores some metadata in our control plane which may be a compliance concern. Legal LOA + certificate signing forms required.

alex: Latency ask: can we hit p50 ~120ms for tiny prompts? They need p90 under 300ms for storefront UX.

spencer: Hosted is best-effort. For p50 ~120ms and tighter p90 you'll want reserved capacity (Dedicated) with a pinned quantized model, batch=1, and prefix caching. If they accept slightly higher p90 we can demo hosted with optimized model and caching.

meera: Pricing calc request: bursty peaks ~1k QPS for 10-30m windows, mixed small messages (avg 40 prompt tokens, 90 response tokens). We'll provide hosted estimate and a Dedicated reserved uplift example. Also include an ops hourly estimate for mTLS management and BYOK attestation.

alex: Action items: Spencer draft a 1-page runbook (SSE NDJSON example, websocket fallback, resumable pattern, function_call handling, sequence-number recovery, Safari keepalive, token-broker pattern) + sample curl snippets and Go websocket example. Meera assemble security appendix & LOA template and list lead times. I'll put together a cost spreadsheet and a short demo plan that uses server token broker for the browser to avoid mid-stream rotation issues.

ci-bot: PR #2001 opened by @spencer - "sse-resume-helper-retry" (CI checks queued).

alex: Great. I'll coordinate a Wed demo with Zephyr (contact: partners@zephyrlogistics.com). Tagging @spencer @meera for follow-ups. :rocket:
